title: Tuna Pasta Salad
subtitle: Fusilli with tinned tuna, sweetcorn, and mayonnaise
excerpt: Fusilli tossed with tinned tuna, sweetcorn, red onion, and celery in a mayonnaise dressing. A British lunchbox and picnic staple. Best made slightly in advance so the pasta absorbs the dressing.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tuna pasta salad is one of the most widely made salads in British households and appears constantly in lunchboxes, picnic baskets, and buffets. The combination of tinned tuna, sweetcorn, and mayonnaise is a well-established British convenience-food classic. Use a good-quality tinned tuna in spring water or olive oil for the best flavour. Dress the pasta while it is still slightly warm for better absorption.

content.text: Cook the pasta until al dente, drain, and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking, then drain thoroughly. Dressing warm pasta makes for a creamier result than cold. The salad keeps well in the fridge for 2 days; thin the dressing with a splash of water when serving if it has dried out.
Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet instruction for al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water until barely warm. Drain thoroughly.
Mix the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, and lemon juice together in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the warm pasta, tuna, sweetcorn, red onion, and celery. Toss until everything is coated. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled.
